fun uri pos fileMap hoverPos cmdStx infoTree caps =>
  match
    Lean.Server.Completion.findPrioritizedCompletionPartitionsAt fileMap hoverPos cmdStx
      infoTree with
  | (prioritizedPartitions, isComplete) =>
    have allCompletions := #[];
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn prioritizedPartitions allCompletions fun partition __s =>
          have allCompletions := __s;
          do
          let __s ←
            forIn partition allCompletions fun x __s =>
                have allCompletions := __s;
                match x with
                | (i, completionInfoPos) => do
                  Lean.Server.CancellableM.checkCancelled
                  have __do_jp :
                    Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem →
                      Lean.Server.CancellableM
                        (ForInStep (Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem)) :=
                    fun completions =>
                    have allCompletions := allCompletions ++ completions;
                    pure (ForInStep.yield allCompletions)
                  match i.info with
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.id stx id danglingDot lctx expectedType? => do
                      let completions ←
                        Lean.Server.Completion.idCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos i.ctx lctx stx
                            id i.hoverInfo danglingDot
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.dot info expectedType? => do
                      let completions ←
                        Lean.Server.Completion.dotCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos i.ctx info
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.dotId stx id lctx expectedType? => do
                      let completions ←
                        Lean.Server.Completion.dotIdCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos i.ctx lctx
                            id expectedType?
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.fieldId stx id lctx structName => do
                      let completions ←
                        Lean.Server.Completion.fieldIdCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos i.ctx
                            lctx id structName
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.option stx => do
                      let completions ←
                        liftM
                            (Lean.Server.Completion.optionCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos i.ctx
                              stx caps)
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.errorName stx partialId => do
                      let completions ←
                        liftM
                            (Lean.Server.Completion.errorNameCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos
                              i.ctx partialId caps)
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.endSection stx id? danglingDot scopeNames => do
                      let completions ←
                        liftM
                            (Lean.Server.Completion.endSectionCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos
                              id? danglingDot scopeNames)
                      __do_jp completions
                    | Lean.Elab.CompletionInfo.tactic stx => do
                      let completions ←
                        liftM
                            (Lean.Server.Completion.tacticCompletion uri pos completionInfoPos
                              i.ctx)
                      __do_jp completions
                    | x => do
                      let completions ← pure #[]
                      __do_jp completions
          have allCompletions : Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem := __s
          if (!allCompletions.isEmpty) = true then pure (ForInStep.done allCompletions)
            else pure (ForInStep.yield allCompletions)
    have allCompletions : Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem := __s
    have finalCompletions : Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem :=
      Lean.Server.Completion.filterDuplicateCompletionItems✝ allCompletions
    pure { isIncomplete := !isComplete, items := finalCompletions }

fun self name moduleUri version refs decls =>

  | some workerRefs =>
    have directImports := workerRefs.directImports;
    have isSetupFailure? := workerRefs.isSetupFailure?;
    match compare version workerRefs.version with
    | Ordering.lt => pure self
    | Ordering.gt =>
      pure
        { ileans := self.ileans,
          workers :=
            Std.TreeMap.insert self.workers name
              { moduleUri := moduleUri, version := version, directImports := directImports,
                isSetupFailure? := isSetupFailure?, refs := refs, decls := decls } }
    | Ordering.eq =>
      have mergedRefs :=
        Std.TreeMap.foldl
          (fun m ident info =>
            Std.TreeMap.insert m ident

    let __do_lift ← Lean.Server.getModuleContainingDecl? ci.env oi.declName

    let __do_lift ← Lean.Server.getModuleContainingDecl? ci.env dei.name

doc:
There are several different identifiers that should be considered equal for the purpose of finding
all references of an identifier:
- `FVarId`s of a function parameter in the function's signature and body
- Chains of helper definitions like those created for do-reassignment `x := e`
- Overlapping definitions like those defined by `where` declarations that define both an FVar
  (for local usage) and a constant (for non-local usage)
- Identifiers connected by `FVarAliasInfo` such as variables before and after `match` generalization

In the first three cases that are not explicitly denoted as aliases with an `FVarAliasInfo`, the
corresponding `Reference`s have the exact same range.
This function finds all definitions that have the exact same range as another definition or usage
and collapses them into a single identifier. It also collapses identifiers connected by
an `FVarAliasInfo`.
When collapsing identifiers, it prefers using a `RefIdent.const name` over a `RefIdent.fvar id` for
all identifiers that are being collapsed into one.

def Lean.Server.combineIdents (trees : Array Lean.Elab.InfoTree) (refs : Array Lean.Server.Reference) :
  Array Lean.Server.Reference

value.text:
fun trees refs =>
  (have posMap := ∅;
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn refs posMap fun ref __s =>
          have posMap := __s;
          match ref with
          |
          { ident := ident, aliases := aliases, range := range, stx := stx, ci := ci, info := info,
              isBinder := true } =>
            have posMap := posMap.insert range ident;
            pure (ForInStep.yield posMap)
          | x => pure (ForInStep.yield posMap)
    have posMap : Std.HashMap Lean.Lsp.Range Lean.Lsp.RefIdent := __s
    have idMap : Std.HashMap Lean.Lsp.RefIdent Lean.Lsp.RefIdent :=
      Lean.Server.combineIdents.useConstRepresentatives✝
        (Lean.Server.combineIdents.buildIdMap✝ trees refs posMap)
    have refs' : Array Lean.Server.Reference := #[]
    let __s ←
      forIn refs refs' fun ref __s =>
          have refs' := __s;
          have id := ref.ident;
          if idMap.contains id = true then
            have refs' :=
              refs'.push
                { ident := Lean.Server.combineIdents.findCanonicalRepresentative✝ idMap id,
                  aliases := #[id], range := ref.range, stx := ref.stx, ci := ref.ci,
                  info := ref.info, isBinder := ref.isBinder };
            pure (ForInStep.yield refs')
          else
            if (!idMap.contains id) = true then
              have refs' := refs'.push ref;
              pure (ForInStep.yield refs')
            else pure (ForInStep.yield refs')
    have refs' : Array Lean.Server.Reference := __s
    refs').run

def Lean.Widget.diffInteractiveGoal✝ (useAfter : Bool) (g₀ : Lean.MVarId)
  (i₁ : Lean.Widget.InteractiveGoal) : Lean.MetaM Lean.Widget.InteractiveGoal

value.text:
fun useAfter g₀ i₁ => do
  let mctx ← Lean.getMCtx
  match mctx.findDecl? g₀ with
    | some md₀ => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
      have lctx₀ : Id Lean.LocalContext :=
        StateT.run' md₀.lctx.sanitizeNames { options := __do_lift }
      let hs₁ ← Lean.Widget.diffHypotheses✝ useAfter lctx₀ i₁.hyps
      have i₁ : Lean.Widget.InteractiveGoal :=
        { hyps := hs₁, type := i₁.type, ctx := i₁.ctx, userName? := i₁.userName?,
          goalPrefix := i₁.goalPrefix, mvarId := i₁.mvarId, isInserted? := i₁.isInserted?,
          isRemoved? := i₁.isRemoved? }
      have g₁ : Lean.MVarId := i₁.mvarId
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType (Lean.Expr.mvar g₀)
      let t₀ ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getMCtx
      match __do_lift.findDecl? g₁ with
        | some md₁ => do
          let t₁ ← Lean.instantiateMVars md₁.type
          let tδ ← Lean.Widget.exprDiff✝ t₀ t₁ useAfter
          let c₁ ← Lean.Widget.addDiffTags✝ useAfter tδ i₁.type
          have i₁ : Lean.Widget.InteractiveGoal :=
            { hyps := i₁.hyps, type := c₁, ctx := i₁.ctx, userName? := i₁.userName?,
              goalPrefix := i₁.goalPrefix, mvarId := i₁.mvarId, isInserted? := some false,
              isRemoved? := i₁.isRemoved? }
          pure i₁
        | x => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "Unknown goal " ++ Lean.toMessageData g₁)
    | x =>
      Lean.throwError
        (Lean.toMessageData "Failed to find decl for " ++ Lean.toMessageData g₀ ++
          Lean.toMessageData ".")

doc:
Computes a diff between `before` and `after` expressions.

This works by recursively comparing function arguments.

TODO(ed): experiment with a 'greatest common subexpression' design where
  given `e₀`, `e₁`, find the greatest common subexpressions `Xs : Array Expr` and a congruence `F` such that
  `e₀ = F[A₀[..Xs]]` and `e₀ = F[A₁[..Xs]]`. Then, we can have fancy diff highlighting where common subexpressions are not highlighted.

## Diffing binders

Two binding domains are identified if they have the same user name and the same type.
The most common tactic that modifies binders is after an `intros`.
To deal with this case, if `before = (a : α) → β` and `after`, is not a matching binder (ie: not `(a : α) → _`)
then we instantiate the `before` variable in a new context and continue diffing `β` against `after`.

fun useAfter ctx₀ h₁ => do
  let __s ←
    forIn (h₁.names.zip h₁.fvarIds) (none, ()) fun x __s =>
        match x with
        | (ppName, fvid) =>
          if (!ctx₀.contains fvid) = true then
            match ctx₀.findFromUserName? (Lean.Name.mkSimple ppName) with
            | some decl₀ => do
              let t₀ ← Lean.instantiateMVars decl₀.type
              let __do_lift ← Lean.Widget.diffHypothesesBundle.withTypeDiff✝ useAfter t₀ h₁
              pure (ForInStep.done (some __do_lift, ()))
            | x =>
              if useAfter = true then
                pure
                  (ForInStep.done
                    (some
                        { names := h₁.names, fvarIds := h₁.fvarIds, type := h₁.type,
                          val? := h₁.val?, isInstance? := h₁.isInstance?, isType? := h₁.isType?,
                          isInserted? := some true, isRemoved? := h₁.isRemoved? },
                      ()))
              else
                pure
                  (ForInStep.done
                    (some
                        { names := h₁.names, fvarIds := h₁.fvarIds, type := h₁.type,
                          val? := h₁.val?, isInstance? := h₁.isInstance?, isType? := h₁.isType?,
                          isInserted? := h₁.isInserted?, isRemoved? := some true },
                      ()))
          else pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
  have __r : Option Lean.Widget.InteractiveHypothesisBundle × Unit := __s
  match __r.1 with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => pure h₁

                        mctx := ti.mctxBefore, options := ci.options,
                        currNamespace := ci.currNamespace, openDecls := ci.openDecls,

    match x with

      have t :=
        (Lean.Language.toSnapshotTree cmdParsed.elabSnap).foldSnaps [] fun snap oldGoals =>
          (match snap.stx? with
            | some stx =>
              match Lean.Server.FileWorker.findGoalsAt?.getPositions✝ stx with
              | some (pos, tailPos, trailingPos) =>
                have snapRange := { start := pos, stop := trailingPos };

                if
                    (!text.rangeContainsHoverPos snapRange hoverPos hasNoTrailingWhitespace) =
                      true then
                  pure
                    (Lean.Server.ServerTask.pure
                      (oldGoals, Lean.Language.SnapshotTree.foldSnaps.Control.proceed false))
                else

                    (Lean.Server.ServerTask.mapCheap
                      (fun tree =>
                        (match tree.element.infoTree? with
                          | some infoTree =>
                            have goals := Lean.Elab.InfoTree.goalsAt? text infoTree hoverPos;

                            else

                          | x =>
                            pure

                      snap.task.asServerTask)
              | x =>
                pure
                  (Lean.Server.ServerTask.pure
                    (oldGoals, Lean.Language.SnapshotTree.foldSnaps.Control.proceed true))
            | x =>
              pure
                (Lean.Server.ServerTask.pure
                  (oldGoals, Lean.Language.SnapshotTree.foldSnaps.Control.proceed false))).run;

        (fun x =>
          match x with
          | [] => none
          | goals => some goals)
        t

doc:
`#click_suggestions` enables a widget in the infoview that gives tactic suggestions for
the expression in the tactic state that was (most recently) selected with shift-click.
Each suggestion has an insert button for pasting it into the editor, at the position of the cursor.

Theorems are searched for use in `apply`, `apply at`, `rw` and `grw`.
These suggestions are grouped and sorted by the pattern that the lemmas match with.
Rewrites that don't change the goal and rewrites that create the same goal as another rewrite
are filtered out, as well as suggestions that create new goal(s) with metavariables in them.
To see all suggestions, click on the filter button (▼) in the top right.

doc:
A congruence lemma between two expressions. The proof is generated dynamically, depending on
whether the resulting lemma should be an `Eq` or a `HEq`.
If generating a proof impossible, then the generator can throw an error.
This can be due to either an `Eq` proof being impossible
or due to the lhs/rhs not being defeq to the lhs/rhs of the generated proof,
which can happen for user-supplied congruence holes.

This complexity is to support two features:

1. The user is free to supply Iff, Eq, and HEq lemmas in congruence holes,
   and we're able to transform them into whatever is appropriate for a
   given congruence lemma.
2. If the congruence hole is a metavariable, then we can specialize that
   hole to an Iff, Eq, or HEq depending on what's necessary at that site.

doc:
Tries to make a congruence between `lhs` and `rhs` automatically.
1. If they are defeq, returns a trivial congruence.
2. Tries using `Subsingleton.elim`.
3. Tries `proof_irrel_heq` as another effort to avoid doing congruence on proofs.
3. Otherwise throws an error.

Note: `mkAppM` uses `withNewMCtxDepth`, which prevents typeclass inference
from accidentally specializing `Sort _` to `Prop`, which could otherwise happen
because there is a `Subsingleton Prop` instance.

  Lean.MetaM Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult

value.text:
fun lhs rhs => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEq lhs rhs
  if __do_lift = true then pure { lhs := lhs, rhs := rhs, pf? := none }
    else do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.observing? (Lean.Meta.mkAppM `Subsingleton.elim #[lhs, rhs])
      match __do_lift with
        | some pf => pure (Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult.mk' lhs rhs pf)
        | x => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.observing? (Lean.Meta.mkAppM `proof_irrel_heq #[lhs, rhs])
          match __do_lift with
            | some pf => pure (Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult.mk' lhs rhs pf)
            | x =>
              Lean.throwError
                (Lean.toMessageData "Could not generate congruence between" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr lhs)) ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "\nand" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr rhs)))

fun mvarCounterSaved lhs rhs =>

    Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.cHole? rhs (some mvarCounterSaved) with
  | some (isLhs1, val1, pf1), some (isLhs2, val2, pf2) =>
    have cls := `Elab.congr;
    do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Option Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult) := fun __r =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType pf1
          let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Meta.inferType pf2
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEq __do_lift __do_lift_1
          have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Option Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult) :=
            fun __r => do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType pf1
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.whnf __do_lift
            have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Option Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult) :=
              fun __r => pure (some (Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult.mk' val1 val2 pf1))
            match __do_lift.sides? with
              | some (fst, lhsVal, fst_1, rhsVal) => do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEq val1 lhsVal
                have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Option Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.CongrResult) :=
                  fun __r => do
                  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isDefEq val2 rhsVal
                  if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
                    else do
                      let __r ←
                        Lean.throwError
                            (Lean.toMessageData "Right-hand side of congruence hole is" ++
                                  Lean.toMessageData
                                    (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr rhsVal)) ++
                                Lean.toMessageData "\nbut is expected to be" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr val2)))
                      __do_jp __r
                if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
                  else do
                    let __r ←
                      Lean.throwError
                          (Lean.toMessageData "Left-hand side of congruence hole is" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData
                                  (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr lhsVal)) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "\nbut is expected to be" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr val1)))
                    __do_jp __r
              | x => __do_jp ()

            else do

                Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.throwCongrEx lhs rhs
                    ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                      "Elaborated types of congruence holes are not defeq.")
              __do_jp __r;
        if (isLhs2 == false) = true then __do_jp ()
        else do

            Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.throwCongrEx lhs rhs
                ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)

          __do_jp __r;
      if (isLhs1 == true) = true then __do_jp ()
      else do
        let __r ←
          Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.throwCongrEx lhs rhs
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "A RHS congruence hole leaked into the LHS")

  | none, some val =>

        "Left-hand side lost its congruence hole annotation.")

doc:
`congr(expr)` generates a congruence from an expression containing
congruence holes of the form `$h` or `$(h)`.
In these congruence holes, `h : a = b` indicates that, in the generated congruence,
on the left-hand side `a` is substituted for `$h`
and on the right-hand side `b` is substituted for `$h`.

For example, if `h : a = b` then `congr(1 + $h) : 1 + a = 1 + b`.

This is able to make use of the expected type, for example `(congr(_ + $h) : 1 + _ = _)`
with `h : x = y` gives `1 + x = 1 + y`.
The expected type can be an `Iff`, `Eq`, or `HEq`.
If there is no expected type, then it generates an equality.

Note: the process of generating a congruence lemma involves elaborating the pattern
using terms with attached metadata and a reducible wrapper.
We try to avoid doing so, but these terms can leak into the local context through unification.
This can potentially break tactics that are sensitive to metadata or reducible functions.
Please report anything that goes wrong with `congr(...)` lemmas on Zulip.

For debugging, you can set `set_option trace.Elab.congr true`.

    have __discr_2 := __discr.getArg 1;
    have __discr := __discr.getArg 2;
    have t := { raw := __discr_2 };
    do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.getMCtx
    have mvarCounterSaved : ℕ := __do_lift.mvarCounter
    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.TermElabM Lean.Expr := fun __r => do
      let lhs ← Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.elaboratePattern t none true
      let rhs ← Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.elaboratePattern t none false
      Lean.Elab.Term.synthesizeSyntheticMVars
      let res ← liftM (Mathlib.Tactic.TermCongr.mkCongrOf 0 mvarCounterSaved lhs rhs)
      let pf ← liftM res.eq
      let ty ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkEq res.lhs res.rhs)
      liftM (Lean.Meta.mkExpectedTypeHint pf ty)
    match expectedType? with
      | some expectedType => do
        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.whnf expectedType)
        match __do_lift.sides? with

doc:
`congr(expr)` generates a congruence from an expression containing
congruence holes of the form `$h` or `$(h)`.
In these congruence holes, `h : a = b` indicates that, in the generated congruence,
on the left-hand side `a` is substituted for `$h`
and on the right-hand side `b` is substituted for `$h`.

For example, if `h : a = b` then `congr(1 + $h) : 1 + a = 1 + b`.

This is able to make use of the expected type, for example `(congr(_ + $h) : 1 + _ = _)`
with `h : x = y` gives `1 + x = 1 + y`.
The expected type can be an `Iff`, `Eq`, or `HEq`.
If there is no expected type, then it generates an equality.

Note: the process of generating a congruence lemma involves elaborating the pattern
using terms with attached metadata and a reducible wrapper.
We try to avoid doing so, but these terms can leak into the local context through unification.
This can potentially break tactics that are sensitive to metadata or reducible functions.
Please report anything that goes wrong with `congr(...)` lemmas on Zulip.

For debugging, you can set `set_option trace.Elab.congr true`.

doc:
`congrm e` is a tactic for proving goals of the form `lhs = rhs`, `lhs ↔ rhs`, `lhs ≍ rhs`,
or `R lhs rhs` when `R` is a reflexive relation.
The expression `e` is a pattern containing placeholders `?_`,
and this pattern is matched against `lhs` and `rhs` simultaneously.
These placeholders generate new goals that state that corresponding subexpressions
in `lhs` and `rhs` are equal.
If the placeholders have names, such as `?m`, then the new goals are given tags with those names.

Examples:
```lean
example {a b c d : ℕ} :
    Nat.pred a.succ * (d + (c + a.pred)) = Nat.pred b.succ * (b + (c + d.pred)) := by
  congrm Nat.pred (Nat.succ ?h1) * (?h2 + ?h3)
  /-  Goals left:
  case h1 ⊢ a = b
  case h2 ⊢ d = b
  case h3 ⊢ c + a.pred = c + d.pred
  -/
  sorry
  sorry
  sorry

example {a b : ℕ} (h : a = b) : (fun y : ℕ => ∀ z, a + a = z) = (fun x => ∀ z, b + a = z) := by
  congrm fun x => ∀ w, ?_ + a = w
  -- ⊢ a = b
  exact h
```

The `congrm` command is a convenient frontend to `congr(...)` congruence quotations.
If the goal is an equality, `congrm e` is equivalent to `refine congr(e')` where `e'` is
built from `e` by replacing each placeholder `?m` by `$(?m)`.
The pattern `e` is allowed to contain `$(...)` expressions to immediately substitute
equality proofs into the congruence, just like for congruence quotations.

doc:
`contrapose` transforms the main goal into its contrapositive. If the goal has the form `⊢ P → Q`,
then `contrapose` turns it into `⊢ ¬ Q → ¬ P`. If the goal has the form `⊢ P ↔ Q`, then `contrapose`
turns it into `⊢ ¬ P ↔ ¬ Q`.

* `contrapose h` on a goal of the form `h : P ⊢ Q` turns the goal into `h : ¬ Q ⊢ ¬ P`. This is
  equivalent to `revert h; contrapose; intro h`.
* `contrapose h with new_h` uses the name `new_h` for the introduced hypothesis. This is equivalent
  to `revert h; contrapose; intro new_h`.
* `contrapose!`, `contrapose! h` and `contrapose! h with new_h` push negation deeper into the goal
  after contraposing (but before introducing the new hypothesis). See the `push Not` tactic for more
  details on the pushing algorithm.
* `contrapose! (config := cfg)` controls the options for negation pushing. All options for
  `Mathlib.Tactic.Push.Config` are supported:
  * `contrapose! +distrib` rewrites `¬ (p ∧ q)` into `¬ p ∨ ¬ q` instead of `p → ¬ q`.

Examples:
```lean4
variables (P Q R : Prop)

example (H : ¬ Q → ¬ P) : P → Q := by
  contrapose
  exact H

example (H : ¬ P ↔ ¬ Q) : P ↔ Q := by
  contrapose
  exact H

example (H : ¬ Q → ¬ P) (h : P) : Q := by
  contrapose h
  exact H h

example (H : ¬ R → P → ¬ Q) : (P ∧ Q) → R := by
  contrapose!
  exact H

example (H : ¬ R → ¬ P ∨ ¬ Q) : (P ∧ Q) → R := by
  contrapose! +distrib
  exact H
```

Analyze strict and permissive trace messages to find isDefEq transition failures
and (optionally) synthesis-grouped failures.
Returns `(flatFailures, synthGroupedFailures)`.

value.text:
fun strictMsgs permMsgs includeSynth =>
  have permSuccesses := ∅;
  have permFailures := ∅;
  do
  let __s ←
    forIn permMsgs (permSuccesses, permFailures) fun msg __s =>
        have permSuccesses := __s.1;
        have permFailures := __s.2;
        do
        let __do_lift ←
          Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.collectIsDefEqChecks✝ (fun x => x == Lean.TraceResult.success)
              msg
        have permSuccesses : Std.HashSet String := permSuccesses.union __do_lift
        let __do_lift ←
          Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.collectIsDefEqChecks✝ (fun x => x == Lean.TraceResult.failure)
              msg
        have permFailures : Std.HashSet String := permFailures.union __do_lift
        pure (ForInStep.yield (permSuccesses, permFailures))
  have permSuccesses : Std.HashSet String := __s.1
  have permFailures : Std.HashSet String := __s.2
  have transitionFailures : Array Lean.MessageData := #[]
  let __s ←
    forIn strictMsgs transitionFailures fun msg __s =>
        have transitionFailures := __s;
        do
        let __do_lift ←
          Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.findTransitionFailures✝ permSuccesses permFailures msg
        have transitionFailures : Array Lean.MessageData := transitionFailures ++ __do_lift
        pure (ForInStep.yield transitionFailures)
  have transitionFailures : Array Lean.MessageData := __s
  let uniqueFailures ← Lean.MessageData.dedupByString transitionFailures
  if (!includeSynth) = true then pure (uniqueFailures, #[])
    else
      have permissiveSuccessApps := ∅;
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn permMsgs permissiveSuccessApps fun msg __s =>
            have permissiveSuccessApps := __s;
            do
            let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.findSynthSuccessApps✝ msg
            have permissiveSuccessApps : Std.HashSet String := permissiveSuccessApps.union __do_lift
            pure (ForInStep.yield permissiveSuccessApps)
      have permissiveSuccessApps : Std.HashSet String := __s
      have synthResults : Array (Lean.MessageData × Array Lean.MessageData) := #[]
      let __s ←
        forIn strictMsgs synthResults fun msg __s =>
            have synthResults := __s;
            do
            let __do_lift ←
              Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.findSynthFailures✝ permSuccesses permFailures msg
            have synthResults : Array (Lean.MessageData × Array Lean.MessageData) :=
              synthResults.append __do_lift
            pure (ForInStep.yield synthResults)
      have synthResults : Array (Lean.MessageData × Array Lean.MessageData) := __s
      let filteredResults ←
        Array.filterM
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (app, snd) => do
                let __do_lift ← app.toString
                pure (permissiveSuccessApps.contains (Lean.MessageData.extractInstName __do_lift)))
            synthResults
      let dedupedResults ←
        Array.mapM
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (app, failures) => do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.MessageData.dedupByString failures
                pure (app, __do_lift))
            filteredResults
      pure (uniqueFailures, dedupedResults)

For failures with syntactically identical LHS and RHS (e.g. `⊤ =?= ⊤`), re-render with
progressively more verbose pp settings to disambiguate. This modifies only the rendering
of the `MessageData` (via `withPPOptions`), not the analysis — the captured `MetavarContext`
and trace structure are preserved, so transition-point detection remains correct.

fun failures =>
  Array.mapM
    (fun f => do
      let __do_lift ← f.toString
      if Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.isIdenticalSidesStr✝ __do_lift = true then do
          let __s ←
            forIn Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.ppEscalations✝ (none, ()) fun ppLevel __s =>
                have escalated := Lean.MessageData.withPPOptions✝ f ppLevel;
                do
                let __do_lift ← escalated.toString
                if Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.isIdenticalSidesStr✝ __do_lift = true then
                    pure (ForInStep.yield (none, ()))
                  else pure (ForInStep.done (some escalated, ()))
          have __r : Option Lean.MessageData × Unit := __s
          match __r.1 with
            | some r => pure r
            | none => pure f
        else pure f)

fun permSuccesses permFailures msg =>

doc:
Collect and combine values of type `α` produced by visiting all trace nodes in a `MessageData`
tree.

Automatically recurses through structural wrappers, invoking `onTrace` only for
`.trace` nodes. The `onTrace` callback receives the arguments of `.trace`:
- the `TraceData` (class name, timing, etc.)
- the trace node's header message
- the trace node's child messages

Each call to `onTrace` is expected to produce either a `descend`, in which case the children of the
trace nodes will be visited, or an `ascend`, in which case they will not. Both may take an argument
`butFirst := some a`, which will cause `a` to be `combine`d into the accumulated value.

We assume `x = combine empty x = combine x empty`. `empty` is attempted to be synthesized as the
`EmptyCollection`, and `combine` is attempted to be synthesized first via the notation `(· ++ ·)`
then via `(· ∪ ·)` as a fallback.

Note that the children may be visited manually via a recursive call to `collectWith` or
`collectWithAndAscend`.

Note: `.ofLazy` nodes are skipped (return `empty`) because they contain unevaluated
formatting thunks, not trace tree structure. This is consistent with `hasTag`
in `Lean.Message` which also skips `.ofLazy`.

    Lean.TraceData → Lean.MessageData → Array Lean.MessageData → m (Lean.MessageData.VisitStep✝ α))
  (empty : α := by exact { })
  (combine : α → α → α := by
    first
    | exact (· ++ ·)
    | exact (· ∪ ·)) :
  m α

def Mathlib.Tactic.DefEqAbuse.reportDefEqAbuse✝ {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadLog m]
  [Lean.AddMessageContext m] [Lean.MonadOptions m] (kind : String)
  (uniqueFailures : Array Lean.MessageData)
  (synthResults : Array (Lean.MessageData × Array Lean.MessageData)) : m Unit

value.text:
fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] [Lean.MonadOptions m] kind
    uniqueFailures synthResults =>
  have failureEmoji := Lean.TraceResult.failure.toEmoji;
  if (!synthResults.isEmpty) = true then
    have entries := #[];
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn synthResults entries fun x __s =>
          have entries := __s;
          match x with
          | (app, failures) =>
            have failureList :=
              Lean.MessageData.joinSep
                (List.map
                  (fun f =>
                    Lean.toMessageData "    " ++ Lean.toMessageData failureEmoji ++
                        Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                      Lean.toMessageData f)
                  failures.toList)
                ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n");
            have entries :=
              entries.push
                (Lean.toMessageData "  " ++ Lean.toMessageData failureEmoji ++
                        Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                      Lean.toMessageData app ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "\n" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData failureList);
            pure (ForInStep.yield entries)
    have entries : Array Lean.MessageData := __s
    have report : Lean.MessageData :=
      Lean.MessageData.joinSep entries.toList ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n")
    Lean.logWarning
        (Lean.toMessageData "#defeq_abuse: " ++ Lean.toMessageData kind ++
            Lean.toMessageData
              " fails with `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency true` but succeeds with `false`.\nThe following synthesis applications fail due to transparency:\n" ++
          Lean.toMessageData report)
  else
    if uniqueFailures.isEmpty = true then
      Lean.logWarning
        (Lean.toMessageData "#defeq_abuse: " ++ Lean.toMessageData kind ++
          Lean.toMessageData
            " fails with `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency true` but succeeds with `false`.\nCould not identify specific failing isDefEq checks from traces.")
    else
      have failureList :=
        Lean.MessageData.joinSep
          (List.map
            (fun f =>
              Lean.toMessageData "  " ++ Lean.toMessageData failureEmoji ++
                  Lean.toMessageData " " ++
                Lean.toMessageData f)
            uniqueFailures.toList)
          ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n");
      Lean.logWarning
        (Lean.toMessageData "#defeq_abuse: " ++ Lean.toMessageData kind ++
            Lean.toMessageData
              " fails with `backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency true` but succeeds with `false`.\nThe following isDefEq checks are the root causes of the failure:\n" ++
          Lean.toMessageData failureList)

doc:
Writing
```lean
deprecate to new_name new_name₂ ... new_nameₙ
theorem old_name : True := .intro
```
where `new_name new_name₂ ... new_nameₙ` is a sequence of identifiers produces the
`Try this` suggestion:
```lean
theorem new_name : True := .intro

@[deprecated (since := "YYYY-MM-DD")] alias old_name := new_name

@[deprecated (since := "YYYY-MM-DD")] alias old_name₂ := new_name₂
...

@[deprecated (since := "YYYY-MM-DD")] alias old_nameₙ := new_nameₙ
```
where `old_name old_name₂ ... old_nameₙ` are the non-blacklisted declarations
(auto)generated by the initial command.

The "YYYY-MM-DD" entry is today's date and it is automatically filled in.

`deprecate to` makes an effort to match `old_name`, the "visible" name, with
`new_name`, the first identifier produced by the user.
The "old", autogenerated declarations `old_name₂ ... old_nameₙ` are retrieved in alphabetical order.
In the case in which the initial declaration produces at most 1 non-blacklisted
declarations besides itself, the alphabetical sorting is irrelevant.

Technically, the command also take an optional `String` argument to fill in the date in `since`.
However, its use is mostly intended for debugging purposes, where having a variable date would
make tests time-dependent.

doc:
`existsi e₁, e₂, ⋯` instantiates existential quantifiers in the main goal by using `e₁`, `e₂`, ...
as witnesses. `existsi e₁, e₂, ⋯` is equivalent to `refine ⟨e₁, e₂, ⋯, ?_⟩`.

See also `exists`: `exists e₁, e₂, ⋯` is equivalent to `existsi e₁, e₂, ⋯; try trivial`.

Examples:

```lean
example : ∃ x : Nat, x = x := by
  existsi 42
  rfl

example : ∃ x : Nat, ∃ y : Nat, x = y := by
  existsi 42, 42
  rfl
```

value.text:
fun t =>
  Lean.Meta.withReducible do
    let t ← Lean.instantiateMVars t
    let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescopeReducing t)
    have head : Lean.HeadIndex := __do_lift.2.2.toHeadIndex
    let pat ← liftM (Lean.Meta.abstractMVars t)
    let env ← Lean.getEnv
    have numFound : ℕ := 0
    let __do_lift ← liftM Mathlib.Tactic.Find.findDeclsPerHead.get
    let _ ←
      forIn (__do_lift.getD head #[]) numFound fun n __s =>
          have numFound := __s;
          have c := (env.find? n).get!;
          do
          let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkFreshLevelMVars c.numLevelParams)
          have cTy : Lean.Expr := c.instantiateTypeLevelParams __do_lift
          let found ←
            Lean.Meta.forallTelescopeReducing cTy fun cParams cTy' => do
                let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkFreshLevelMVars pat.numMVars)
                have pat : Lean.Expr :=
                  pat.expr.instantiateLevelParamsArray pat.paramNames __do_lift.toArray
                let __x ← liftM (Lean.Meta.lambdaMetaTelescope pat)
                match __x with
                  | (fst, fst_1, pat) => do
                    let __x ← liftM (Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescopeReducing pat)
                    match __x with
                      | (patParams, fst, pat) =>
                        liftM (Lean.Meta.isDefEq cTy' pat) <&&>
                          liftM (Mathlib.Tactic.Find.matchHyps✝ patParams.toList [] cParams.toList)
          if found = true then
              have numFound := numFound + 1;
              if numFound > 20 then do
                Lean.logInfo (Lean.toMessageData "maximum number of search results reached")
                pure (ForInStep.done numFound)
              else do
                Lean.logInfo
                    (Lean.toMessageData n ++ Lean.toMessageData ": " ++ Lean.toMessageData cTy)
                pure (ForInStep.yield numFound)
            else pure (ForInStep.yield numFound)
    pure ()

fun tacticCode e =>
  Lean.withTraceNode `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop

value.text:
fun declName => do
  let info ← Lean.getConstInfo declName
  let __x ← Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescope info.type
  match __x with
    | (xs, bi, b) =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r =>
        have lvls := List.map (fun l => Lean.Level.param l) info.levelParams;
        have e := Lean.mkAppN (Lean.Expr.const declName lvls) xs;
        do
        let path ← Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.mkPath e
        let __x ←
          Array.findIdxM?
              (fun x =>
                match x with
                | (x, bi) => do
                  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType x
                  if (__do_lift.isForall && bi.isExplicit) = true then pure true else pure false)
              (xs.zip bi)
        match __x with
          | some funArgId =>
            have funArgId := funArgId;
            have decl := { funPropName := declName, path := path, funArgId := funArgId };
            do
            Lean.modifyEnv fun env =>
                Lean.ScopedEnvExtension.addEntry Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.funPropDeclsExt env decl
            have cls : Lean.Name := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop.attr
            let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
            if __do_lift = true then
                Lean.addTrace cls
                  (Lean.toMessageData "added new function property `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData declName ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "`\nlook up pattern is `" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData path ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "`")
              else pure ()
          | x =>
            Lean.throwError
              (Lean.toMessageData
                "invalid fun_prop declaration, can't find argument of type `α → β`");
      if ¬b.isProp = true then do
        let __r ←
          Lean.throwError
              (Lean.toMessageData "invalid fun_prop declaration, has to be `Prop`-valued function")
        __do_jp __r
      else __do_jp ()

fun f unfoldPred =>
  Lean.Meta.withConfig
    (fun cfg =>
      { foApprox := cfg.foApprox, ctxApprox := cfg.ctxApprox,
        quasiPatternApprox := cfg.quasiPatternApprox, constApprox := cfg.constApprox,
        isDefEqStuckEx := cfg.isDefEqStuckEx, unificationHints := cfg.unificationHints,
        proofIrrelevance := cfg.proofIrrelevance,
        assignSyntheticOpaque := cfg.assignSyntheticOpaque, offsetCnstrs := cfg.offsetCnstrs,
        transparency := cfg.transparency, etaStruct := cfg.etaStruct, univApprox := cfg.univApprox,
        iota := cfg.iota, beta := cfg.beta, proj := cfg.proj, zeta := false, zetaDelta := false,
        zetaUnused := cfg.zetaUnused, zetaHave := cfg.zetaHave })
    (have unfold := fun e =>
      match e.getAppFn'.constName? with
      | some n => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.isReducible n
        pure (unfoldPred n || __do_lift)
      | x => pure false;
    do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType f
    let __x ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
    match __x with
      | Lean.Expr.forallE xName xType body binderInfo =>
        Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD xName xType fun x => do
          let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.whnfPred (f.beta #[x]).eta unfold
          have fx' : Lean.Expr := Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.headBetaThroughLet __do_lift
          let f' ← Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[x] fx'
          match fx' with
            | Lean.Expr.letE declName type value body nondep =>
              pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MaybeFunctionData.letE f')
            | Lean.Expr.lam binderName binderType body binderInfo =>
              pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MaybeFunctionData.lam f')
            | x => do
              let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getFunctionData f'
              pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MaybeFunctionData.data __do_lift)
      | x => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType f
        let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Meta.inferType f
        Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData "fun_prop bug: function expected, got `" ++ Lean.toMessageData f ++
                    Lean.toMessageData " : " ++
                  Lean.toMessageData __do_lift ++
                Lean.toMessageData ", type ctor " ++
              Lean.toMessageData __do_lift_1.ctorName))

Decompose function `fun x ↦ f y₁ ... yₙ` over specified argument indices `#[i, j, ...]`.

The result is:
```
(fun (yᵢ',yⱼ',...) ↦ f y₁ .. yᵢ' .. yⱼ' .. yₙ) ∘ (fun x ↦ (yᵢ, yⱼ, ...))
```

fun fData args =>
  if Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.isOrderedSubsetOf fData.mainArgs args = true then
    if ¬fData.fn.containsFVar fData.mainVar.fvarId! = true then
      Lean.Meta.withLCtx fData.lctx fData.insts
        (have gxs := Array.map (fun i => fData.args[i]!.expr) args;
        do
        let e ←
          tryCatch
              (do
                let gx ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.mkProdElem gxs
                let g ←
                  Lean.Meta.withLCtx fData.lctx fData.insts
                      (Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[fData.mainVar] gx)
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType gx
                let r ←
                  Lean.Meta.withLocalDeclD `y __do_lift fun y => do
                      let ys ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.mkProdSplitElem y gxs.size
                      have args' : Array Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.Arg :=
                        Array.foldl
                          (fun args' x =>
                            match x with
                            | (i, y) => args'.set! i { expr := y, coe := args'[i]!.coe })
                          fData.args (args.zip ys)
                      let f ←
                        Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[y]
                            (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.mkAppN fData.fn args')
                      pure (some (f, g))
                ExceptT.run (pure r))
              fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
        EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r)
    else pure none
  else pure none

fun f =>
  have __do_jp := fun __r =>
    match h : f.args.size with
    | 0 => pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.none
    | n.succ =>
      if f.args[n].coe.isSome = true then pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.exact
      else
        if (f.args.any fun a => a.coe.isSome) = true then
          pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.overApplied
        else pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.none;
  match f.fn.constName? with

    if __do_lift = true then do
        let info ← Lean.getConstInfo name
        have arity : ℕ := info.type.getNumHeadForalls
        match compare arity f.args.size with
          | Ordering.eq => pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.exact
          | Ordering.lt => pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.overApplied
          | Ordering.gt => pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.underApplied
      else __do_jp ()
  | x => __do_jp ()

    have xId := xs[0]!.fvarId!;
    Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.withApp b fun fn args =>
      have fn := fn;
      have args := args;
      have __do_jp := fun __r fn args =>
        have mainArgs :=
          Array.filterMap id
            (Array.mapIdx
              (fun i x =>
                match x with
                | { expr := arg, coe := coe } =>
                  if arg.containsFVar xId = true then some i else none)
              args);
        do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.getLCtx
        let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.Meta.getLocalInstances
        pure
            { lctx := __do_lift, insts := __do_lift_1, fn := fn, args := args, mainVar := xs[0]!,
              mainArgs := mainArgs };
      match fn with
      | Lean.Expr.proj n i x => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
        match Lean.getStructureInfo? __do_lift n with
          | some info =>
            match info.getProjFn? i with
            | some projName => do
              let p ← Lean.Meta.mkAppM projName #[x]
              have fn : Lean.Expr := p.getAppFn
              have args : Array Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.Arg :=
                Array.map (fun a => { expr := a }) p.getAppArgs ++ args
              __do_jp () fn args
            | x => do
              let __r ←
                panicWithPosWithDecl "Mathlib.Tactic.FunProp.FunctionData"
                    "Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getFunctionData" 89 49 "unreachable code has been reached"
              __do_jp __r fn args
          | x => do
            let __r ←
              panicWithPosWithDecl "Mathlib.Tactic.FunProp.FunctionData"
                  "Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getFunctionData" 88 58 "unreachable code has been reached"

doc:
Decomposes `fun x ↦ f y₁ ... yₙ` into `(fun g ↦ g yₙ) ∘ (fun x y ↦ f y₁ ... yₙ₋₁ y)`

Returns `DecompositionResult.failed` if:
- `n=0`
- `yₙ` contains `x`
- `n=1` and `(fun x y ↦ f y)` is identity function i.e. `x=f`

signature.text:
def Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunctionData.peeloffArgDecomposition
  (fData : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunctionData) : Lean.MetaM Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult

value.text:
fun fData =>
  if fData.args.size > 0 then
    Lean.Meta.withLCtx fData.lctx fData.insts
      (have n := fData.args.size;
      have x := fData.mainVar;
      have yₙ := fData.args[n - 1]!;
      if yₙ.expr.containsFVar x.fvarId! = true then
        pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult.failed
      else
        if (decide (fData.args.size = 1) && fData.mainVar == fData.fn) = true then
          pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult.failed
        else
          have gBody' :=
            Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Mor.mkAppN fData.fn ↑(fData.args.toSubarray 0 (n - 1));
          have gBody' :=
            match yₙ.coe with
            | some coe => coe.app gBody'
            | x => gBody';
          do
          let g' ← Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars #[x] gBody'
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType gBody'
          have f' : Lean.Expr := Lean.Expr.lam `f __do_lift ((Lean.Expr.bvar 0).app yₙ.expr) default
          pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult.comp f' g'))
  else pure Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult.failed

doc: Increase transition depth. Return `none` if maximum transition depth has been reached.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.withIncreasedTransitionDepth {α : Type}
  (go : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option α)) : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option α)

value.text:
fun {α} go => do
  let __do_lift ← read
  have maxDepth : ℕ := __do_lift.config.maxTransitionDepth
  let __do_lift ← read
  have newDepth : ℕ := __do_lift.transitionDepth + 1
  if newDepth > maxDepth then
      have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop;
      do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      have __do_jp : Unit → Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option α) := fun __r => pure none
      if __do_lift = true then do
          let __r ←
            Lean.addTrace cls
                (Lean.toMessageData "maximum transition depth (" ++ Lean.toMessageData maxDepth ++
                      Lean.toMessageData
                        ") reached\n    if you want `fun_prop` to continue then increase the maximum depth with `fun_prop (maxTransitionDepth := " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData newDepth ++
                  Lean.toMessageData ")`")
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
    else
      withReader
        (fun s =>
          { config := s.config, constToUnfold := s.constToUnfold, disch := s.disch,
            transitionDepth := newDepth })
        go

Log error message that will displayed to the user at the end.

Messages are logged only when `transitionDepth = 0` i.e. when `fun_prop` is **not** trying to infer
function property like continuity from another property like differentiability.
The main reason is that if the user forgets to add a continuity theorem for function `foo` then
`fun_prop` should report that there is a continuity theorem for `foo` missing. If we would log
messages `transitionDepth > 0` then user will see messages saying that there is a missing theorem
for differentiability, smoothness, ... for `foo`.

  let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getTheoremFromConst declName prio

      have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop.attr;

      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Unit := fun __r =>
        Lean.ScopedEnvExtension.add Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.lambdaTheoremsExt thm attrKind

          let __r ←
            Lean.addTrace cls
                (Lean.toMessageData "lambda theorem: " ++ Lean.toMessageData thm.thmName ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "\nfunction property: " ++
                      Lean.toMessageData thm.funPropName ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "\ntype: " ++
                  Lean.toMessageData (repr thm.thmArgs.type))

      have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop.attr;

      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Unit := fun __r =>

doc: Decides whether `f` is a function corresponding to one of the lambda theorems.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.detectLambdaTheoremArgs (f : Lean.Expr) (ctxVars : Array Lean.Expr) :
  Lean.MetaM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs)

value.text:
fun f ctxVars => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType f
  let f ←
    Lean.Meta.forallTelescope __do_lift fun xs x =>
        Lean.Meta.mkLambdaFVars xs (Lean.mkAppN f xs).headBeta
  match f with
    | Lean.Expr.lam binderName binderType xBody binderInfo =>
      if xBody.hasLooseBVars = true then
        match xBody with
        | Lean.Expr.bvar 0 => pure (some Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs.id)
        | (Lean.Expr.bvar 0).app (Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId) =>
          pure (some Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs.apply)
        | (Lean.Expr.fvar fId).app ((Lean.Expr.fvar gId).app (Lean.Expr.bvar 0)) =>
          match Array.findIdx? (fun x => x == Lean.Expr.fvar fId) ctxVars with
          | some argId_f =>
            match Array.findIdx? (fun x => x == Lean.Expr.fvar gId) ctxVars with
            | some argId_g =>
              pure (some (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs.comp argId_f argId_g))
            | x => pure none
          | x => pure none
        |
        Lean.Expr.lam binderName binderType
            (((Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId).app (Lean.Expr.bvar 1)).app (Lean.Expr.bvar 0)) binderInfo =>
          pure (some Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs.pi)
        | x => pure none
      else pure (some Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.LambdaTheoremArgs.const)
    | x => pure none

doc:
For a theorem declaration `declName` return `fun_prop` theorem. It correctly detects which
type of theorem it is.

signature.text:
def Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getTheoremFromConst (declName : Lean.Name) (prio : ℕ := 1000) :
  Lean.MetaM Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem

value.text:
fun declName prio => do
  let info ← Lean.getConstInfo declName
  Lean.Meta.forallTelescope info.type fun xs b => do
      let __x ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getFunProp? b
      match __x with
        | some (decl, f) =>
          have funPropName := decl.funPropName;
          do
          let fData? ←
            Lean.Meta.withConfig
                (fun cfg =>
                  { foApprox := cfg.foApprox, ctxApprox := cfg.ctxApprox,
                    quasiPatternApprox := cfg.quasiPatternApprox, constApprox := cfg.constApprox,
                    isDefEqStuckEx := cfg.isDefEqStuckEx, unificationHints := cfg.unificationHints,
                    proofIrrelevance := cfg.proofIrrelevance,
                    assignSyntheticOpaque := cfg.assignSyntheticOpaque,
                    offsetCnstrs := cfg.offsetCnstrs, transparency := cfg.transparency,
                    etaStruct := cfg.etaStruct, univApprox := cfg.univApprox, iota := cfg.iota,
                    beta := cfg.beta, proj := cfg.proj, zeta := false, zetaDelta := cfg.zetaDelta,
                    zetaUnused := cfg.zetaUnused, zetaHave := cfg.zetaHave })
                (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getFunctionData? f Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.defaultUnfoldPred)
          let __do_lift ← fData?.get
          let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.detectLambdaTheoremArgs __do_lift xs
          match __do_lift with
            | some thmArgs =>
              pure
                (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem.lam
                  { funPropName := funPropName, thmName := declName, thmArgs := thmArgs })
            | x =>
              match fData? with
              | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MaybeFunctionData.data fData =>
                match fData.fn with
                | Lean.Expr.const funName us => do
                  let dec ← fData.decomposition
                  pure
                      (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem.function
                        { funPropName := funPropName,
                          thmOrigin := Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Origin.decl declName,
                          funOrigin := Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Origin.decl funName,
                          mainArgs := fData.mainArgs, appliedArgs := fData.args.size,
                          priority := prio, form := dec.toTheoremForm })
                | Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId => do
                  let __x ← Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescope info.type
                  match __x with
                    | (fst, fst_1, b') => do
                      let keys ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.initializeLazyEntryWithEta b'
                      have thm : Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.GeneralTheorem :=
                        { funPropName := funPropName, thmName := declName, keys := keys,
                          priority := prio }
                      let __do_lift ← fData.isMorApplication
                      match __do_lift with
                        | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.exact =>
                          pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem.mor thm)
                        | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.overApplied =>
                          pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem.mor thm)
                        | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.underApplied =>
                          Lean.throwError
                            (Lean.toMessageData
                              "fun_prop theorem about morphism coercion has to be in fully applied form")
                        | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.none =>
                          if
                              (fData.fn.isFVar && fData.args.size == 1 &&
                                  fData.args[0]!.expr == fData.mainVar) =
                                true then
                            pure (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Theorem.transition thm)
                          else
                            Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "Not a valid `fun_prop` theorem!")
                | x => do
                  let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr b
                  Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "unrecognized theoremType `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData __do_lift ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "`")
              | x => do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr f
                Lean.throwError
                    ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                      (toString "function in invalid form " ++ toString __do_lift))
        | x => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.ppExpr b
          Lean.throwError
              (Lean.toMessageData "unrecognized function property `" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData __do_lift ++
                Lean.toMessageData "`")

doc:
There are four types of theorems:
- lam - theorem about basic lambda calculus terms
- function - theorem about a specific function(declared or free variable) in specific arguments
- mor - special theorems talking about bundled morphisms/DFunLike.coe
- transition - theorems inferring one function property from another

Examples:
- lam
  ```
  theorem Continuous_id : Continuous fun x ↦ x
  theorem Continuous_comp (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) : Continuous fun x ↦ f (g x)
  ```
- function
  ```
  theorem Continuous_add : Continuous (fun x ↦ x.1 + x.2)
  theorem Continuous_add (hf : Continuous f) (hg : Continuous g) :
      Continuous (fun x ↦ (f x) + (g x))
  ```
- mor - the head of function body has to be `DFunLike.coe`
  ```
  theorem ContDiff.clm_apply {f : E → F →L[𝕜] G} {g : E → F}
      (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 n f) (hg : ContDiff 𝕜 n g) :
      ContDiff 𝕜 n fun x ↦ (f x) (g x)
  theorem clm_linear {f : E →L[𝕜] F} : IsLinearMap 𝕜 f
  ```
- transition - the conclusion has to be in the form `P f` where `f` is a free variable
  ```
  theorem linear_is_continuous [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {f : E → F} (hf : IsLinearMap 𝕜 f) :
      Continuous f
  ```

fun funPropDecl e fData funProp =>
  match fData.fn.const? with
  | some (funName, snd) => do
    let globalThms ←
      liftM
          (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getDeclTheorems funPropDecl funName fData.mainArgs fData.args.size)
    have cls : Lean.Name := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop
    let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
    have __do_jp : Unit → Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) :=
      fun __r => do
      let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.tryTheorems funPropDecl e fData globalThms funProp
      match __do_lift with
        | some r => pure (some r)
        | x => do
          let localThms ←
            Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.getLocalTheorems funPropDecl
                (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Origin.decl funName) fData.mainArgs fData.args.size
          have __do_jp :
            Unit → Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) := fun __r =>
            do
            let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.tryTheorems funPropDecl e fData localThms funProp
            match __do_lift with
              | some r => pure (some r)
              | x =>
                have __do_jp := fun __r => do
                  let __do_lift ← liftM fData.isMorApplication
                  have __do_jp :
                    Unit → Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) :=
                    fun __r => do
                    let __do_lift ← liftM fData.decomposition
                    have __do_jp :
                      Unit → Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) :=
                      fun __r => pure none
                    match __do_lift with
                      | Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.DecompositionResult.comp f g =>
                        have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop;
                        do
                        let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
                        have __do_jp :
                          Unit →
                            Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) :=
                          fun __r => do
                          let __do_lift ←
                            Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.applyCompRule funPropDecl e f g funProp
                          match __do_lift with
                            | some r => pure (some r)
                            | x => __do_jp ()
                        if __do_lift = true then do
                            let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.ppExpr f)
                            let __do_lift_1 ← liftM (Lean.Meta.ppExpr g)
                            let __r ←
                              Lean.addTrace cls
                                  ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                                    (toString "failed applying `" ++
                                                    toString funPropDecl.funPropName ++
                                                  toString "` theorems for `" ++
                                                toString funName ++
                                              toString
                                                "`\n         trying again after decomposing function as: `(" ++
                                            toString __do_lift ++
                                          toString ") ∘ (" ++
                                        toString __do_lift_1 ++
                                      toString ")`"))
                            __do_jp __r
                          else __do_jp ()
                      | x =>
                        have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop;
                        do
                        let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
                        have __do_jp :
                          Unit →
                            Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.FunPropM (Option Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.Result) :=
                          fun __r => do
                          let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.applyTransitionRules e funProp
                          match __do_lift with
                            | some r => pure (some r)
                            | x => __do_jp ()
                        if __do_lift = true then do
                            let __r ←
                              Lean.addTrace cls
                                  ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                                    (toString "failed applying `" ++
                                                toString funPropDecl.funPropName ++
                                              toString "` theorems for `" ++
                                            toString funName ++
                                          toString "`\n         now trying to prove `" ++
                                        toString funPropDecl.funPropName ++
                                      toString "` from another function property"))
                            __do_jp __r
                          else __do_jp ()
                  if (__do_lift != Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.MorApplication.none) = true then do
                      let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.applyMorRules funPropDecl e fData funProp
                      match __do_lift with
                        | some r => pure (some r)
                        | x => __do_jp ()
                    else __do_jp ();
                if (decide (globalThms.size = 0) && decide (localThms.size = 0)) = true then do
                  let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.ppExpr e)
                  let __r ←
                    Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.logError
                        (toString "No theorems found for `" ++ toString funName ++
                              toString "` in order to prove `" ++
                            toString __do_lift ++
                          toString "`")
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ()
          if localThms.size ≠ 0 then
              have cls := `Meta.Tactic.fun_prop;
              do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
              if __do_lift = true then do
                  let __do_lift ←
                    Array.mapM (fun thm => liftM (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.ppOrigin' thm.thmOrigin))
                        localThms
                  let __r ←
                    Lean.addTrace cls
                        ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                          (toString "candidate local theorems for " ++ toString funName ++
                              toString " " ++
                            toString __do_lift))
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ()
            else __do_jp ()
    if __do_lift = true then do
        let __do_lift ←
          Array.mapM (fun thm => liftM (Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.ppOrigin' thm.thmOrigin)) globalThms
        let __r ←
          Lean.addTrace cls
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                (toString "candidate theorems for " ++ toString funName ++ toString " " ++
                  toString __do_lift))
        __do_jp __r
      else __do_jp ()
  | x => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "fun_prop bug: invelid use of const app case")

doc:
`fun_prop` solves a goal of the form `P f`, where `P` is a predicate and `f` is a function,
by decomposing `f` into a composition of elementary functions, and proving `P` on each of those
by matching against a set of `@[fun_prop]` lemmas.

If `fun_prop` fails to solve a goal with the error "No theorems found", you can solve this issue
by importing or adding new theorems tagged with the `@[fun_prop]` attribute. See the module
documentation for `Mathlib/Tactic/FunProp.lean` for a detailed explanation.

* `fun_prop (disch := tac)` uses `tac` to solve potential side goals. Setting this option is
  required to solve `ContinuousAt/On/Within` goals. Assumptions from the local context are
  automatically discharged.
* `fun_prop [c, ...]` will unfold the constant(s) `c`, ... before decomposing `f`.
* `fun_prop (config := cfg)` sets advanced configuration options using `cfg : FunProp.Config`
  (see `FunProp.Config` for details).
  These options can be combined: `fun_prop (config := cfg) (disch := tac) [c]`

Examples:

```lean
example : Continuous (fun x : ℝ ↦ x * sin x) := by fun_prop
```

```lean
-- Solving `ContinuousAt`/`Within`/`On` goals might require using dischargers:
example (y : ℝ) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ContinuousAt (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1/x) y := by
  fun_prop

example (y : ℝ) (hy : y ≠ 0) : ContinuousAt (fun x => x * (Real.log x) ^ 2 - Real.exp x / x) y := by
  fun_prop (disch := aesop)
```

`Nondet m α` is variation on `MLList m α` suitable for use with backtrackable monads `m`.

We think of `Nondet m α` as a nondeterministic value in `α`,
with the possible alternatives stored in a monadic lazy list.

Along with each `a : α` we store the backtrackable state, and ensure that monadic operations
on alternatives run with the appropriate state.

Operations on the nondeterministic value via `bind`, `mapM`, and `filterMapM`
run with the appropriate backtrackable state, and are responsible for updating the state themselves
(typically this doesn't need to be done explicitly,
but just happens as a side effect in the monad `m`).

fun {σ} {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadBacktrack σ m] =>

    map := fun {α β} f x =>
      (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) x ((fun {α} a => Nondet.singletonM (pure a)) ∘ f),
    pure := fun {α} a => Nondet.singletonM (pure a),
    seq := fun {α β} f x =>
      (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) f fun y =>
        (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) (x ()) ((fun {α} a => Nondet.singletonM (pure a)) ∘ y),
    seqLeft := fun {α β} x y =>
      (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) x fun a =>
        (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) (y ()) fun x => (fun {α} a => Nondet.singletonM (pure a)) a,
    seqRight := fun {α β} x y => (fun {α β} => Nondet.bind) x fun x => y (),
    failure := fun {α} => Nondet.nil,
    orElse := fun {α} x y => { toMLList := x.toMLList.append fun x => (y ()).toMLList },
    bind := fun {α β} => Nondet.bind }

doc:
Run all tactics registered using `register_hint`.
Print a "Try these:" suggestion for each of the successful tactics.

If one tactic succeeds and closes the goal, we don't look at subsequent tactics.

signature.text: def Mathlib.Tactic.Hint.hint (stx : Lean.Syntax) : Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Unit

value.text:
fun stx =>
  Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext do
    let __do_lift ← liftM Mathlib.Tactic.Hint.getHints
    have tacs : List (Lean.TSyntax `tactic) :=
      List.map (fun x => x.2) (__do_lift.toArray.qsort fun x1 x2 => decide (x1.1 > x2.1)).toList
    have tacs : Nondet Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM (Lean.TSyntax `tactic) := Nondet.ofList tacs
    have results :
      Nondet Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM (List Lean.MVarId × Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion) :=
      Nondet.filterMapM
        (fun t => do
          let __do_lift ←
            Lean.observing? (Mathlib.Tactic.withResetServerInfo (Lean.Elab.Tactic.evalTactic t.raw))
          match __do_lift with
            | some { result? := result?, msgs := msgs, trees := trees } =>
              if msgs.hasErrors = true then pure none
              else do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getGoals
                let __do_lift_1 ← Mathlib.Tactic.Hint.suggestion t trees
                pure (some (__do_lift, __do_lift_1))
            | x => pure none)
        tacs
    let results ← (results.toMLList.takeUpToFirst fun r => r.1.1.isEmpty).asArray
    have results :
      Array
        ((List Lean.MVarId × Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion) × Lean.Elab.Tactic.SavedState) :=
      results.qsort fun x1 x2 => decide (x1.1.1.length < x2.1.1.length)
    liftM (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.addSuggestions stx (Array.map (fun x => x.1.2) results))
    match Array.find? (fun x => x.1.1.isEmpty) results with
      | some r => Lean.setMCtx r.2.term.meta.meta.mctx
      | none => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getMainGoal
        liftM (Lean.Elab.admitGoal __do_lift)

doc:
Construct a suggestion for a tactic.
* Check the passed `MessageLog` for an info message beginning with "Try this: ".
* If found, use that as the suggestion.
* Otherwise use the provided syntax.
* Also, look for remaining goals and pretty print them after the suggestion.

value.text:
fun tac trees => do
  let goals ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getGoals
  have __do_jp : Option String → Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion :=
    fun postInfo? =>
    have preInfo? := if goals.isEmpty = true then some "🎉️ " else none;
    have suggestions := Lean.Elab.collectTryThisSuggestions trees;
    have suggestion :=
      match suggestions[0]? with
      | some s => s.suggestion
      | none => Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionText.tsyntax tac;
    pure { suggestion := suggestion, preInfo? := preInfo?, postInfo? := postInfo? }
  if goals.isEmpty = true then do
      let postInfo? ← pure none
      __do_jp postInfo?
    else
      have str := "\nRemaining subgoals:";
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn goals str fun g __s =>
            have str := __s;
            do
            let __do_lift ← liftM g.getType
            let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
            let e ← liftM (Lean.PrettyPrinter.ppExpr __do_lift)
            have str : String := str ++ (Std.Format.text "\n⊢ " ++ e).pretty
            pure (ForInStep.yield str)
      have str : String := __s
      let postInfo? ← pure (some str)
      __do_jp postInfo?

    Lean.throwError
      (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
        Lean.toMessageData "` is not marked with the `[grind]` attribute");

  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv

      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.getEqnsFor? declName

          if (eqns.all fun eqn => s.contains (Lean.Meta.Grind.Origin.decl eqn)) = true then
            __do_jp ()
          else do
            let __r ← throwErr
            __do_jp __r
        | x => throwErr
    else
      have __do_jp := fun __r => pure (s.erase (Lean.Meta.Grind.Origin.decl declName));
      if s.contains (Lean.Meta.Grind.Origin.decl declName) = true then __do_jp ()

value.text:
fun declName => do
  let info ← Lean.getConstVal declName
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM Lean.Expr := fun __r =>
    have us := List.map Lean.mkLevelParam info.levelParams;
    pure (Lean.mkConst declName us)
  if Lean.wasOriginallyTheorem __do_lift declName = true then __do_jp ()
    else do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isProp info.type
      if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
        else do
          let __r ←
            Lean.throwError
                (Lean.toMessageData "invalid `grind` theorem `" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                  Lean.toMessageData "`, type is not a proposition")
          __do_jp __r

Inserts a `thm` with symbols `[s_1, ..., s_n]` to `s`.
We add `s_1 -> { thm with symbols := [s_2, ..., s_n] }`.
When `grind` internalizes a term containing symbol `s`, we

def Lean.Meta.Grind.getProofWithFreshMVarLevels {α : Type} [Lean.Meta.Grind.TheoremLike α] (thm : α) :
  Lean.MetaM Lean.Expr

value.text:
fun {α} [Lean.Meta.Grind.TheoremLike α] thm =>
  have proof := Lean.Meta.Grind.TheoremLike.getProof thm;
  have us := Lean.Meta.Grind.TheoremLike.getLevelParams thm;
  if (proof.isConst && us.isEmpty) = true then
    have declName := proof.constName!;
    do
    let info ← Lean.getConstVal declName
    if info.levelParams.isEmpty = true then pure proof
      else Lean.Meta.mkConstWithFreshMVarLevels declName
  else
    if us.isEmpty = true then pure proof
    else do
      let us' ← Array.mapM (fun x => Lean.Meta.mkFreshLevelMVar) us
      pure (proof.instantiateLevelParamsArray us us')

doc:
Incremental variant of `shareCommonAlpha` for expressions constructed from already-shared subterms.

Use this when an expression `e` was produced by a Lean API (e.g., `inferType`, `mkApp4`) that
does not preserve maximal sharing, but the inputs to that API were already maximally shared.
In this case, only the newly constructed nodes need processing—the shared subterms can be
looked up directly in the `AlphaShareCommonM` state without building a temporary hashmap.

Unlike `shareCommonAlpha`, this function does not use a local `Std.HashMap ExprPtr Expr` to
track visited nodes. This is more efficient when the number of new (unshared) nodes is small,
which is the common case when wrapping API calls that build a few constructor nodes around
shared inputs.

Example:
```
-- `a` and `b` are already maximally shared
let result := mkApp2 f a b  -- result is not maximally shared
let result ← shareCommonAlphaInc result -- efficiently restore sharing
```

Incremental variant of `shareCommon` for expressions constructed from already-shared subterms.

Use this when an expression `e` was produced by a Lean API (e.g., `inferType`, `mkApp4`) that
does not preserve maximal sharing, but the inputs to that API were already maximally shared.

Unlike `shareCommon`, this function does not use a local `Std.HashMap ExprPtr Expr` to
track visited nodes. This is more efficient when the number of new (unshared) nodes is small,
which is the common case when wrapping API calls that build a few constructor nodes around
shared inputs.

Example:
```
-- `a` and `b` are already maximally shared
let result := mkApp2 f a b  -- result is not maximally shared
let result ← shareCommonInc result -- efficiently restore sharing
```

fun s =>
  have __do_jp := fun msg => do
    let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
    let scp ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
    let quotCtx ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
    pure
        {
          raw :=
            Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Term.doExpr
              (Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Term.app
                (Lean.Syntax.ident info "Sym.reportDbgIssue".toRawSubstring'
                  (Lean.addMacroScope quotCtx `Sym.reportDbgIssue scp)
                  [Lean.Syntax.Preresolved.decl `Lean.Meta.Sym.reportDbgIssue []])
                (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `null msg.raw)) };
  if (s.getKind == Lean.interpolatedStrKind) = true then do
    let msg ←
      do
        let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
        let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
        let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
        pure
            {
              raw :=
                Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.termM!_ (Lean.Syntax.atom info "m!") { raw := s }.raw }
    __do_jp msg
  else do
    let msg ←
      do
        let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
        let scp ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
        let quotCtx ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
        pure
            {
              raw :=
                Lean.Syntax.node5 info `Lean.Parser.Term.typeAscription
                  (Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Term.hygienicLParen
                    (Lean.Syntax.atom info "(")
                    (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `hygieneInfo
                      (Lean.Syntax.ident info "".toRawSubstring'
                        (Lean.addMacroScope quotCtx Lean.Name.anonymous scp)
                        [Lean.Syntax.Preresolved.namespace `Lean.Meta.Sym])))
                  { raw := s }.raw (Lean.Syntax.atom info ":")
                  (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `null
                    (Lean.Syntax.ident info "MessageData".toRawSubstring'
                      (Lean.addMacroScope quotCtx `MessageData scp)
                      [Lean.Syntax.Preresolved.decl `Lean.MessageData [],
                        Lean.Syntax.Preresolved.namespace `Lean.MessageData]))
                  (Lean.Syntax.atom info ")") }
    __do_jp msg

doc:
Maps expressions to their maximal free variable (by declaration index).

- `maxFVar[e] = some fvarId` means `fvarId` is the free variable with the largest declaration
  index occurring in `e`.
- `maxFVar[e] = none` means `e` contains no free variables (but may contain metavariables).

Recall that if `e` contains a metavariable `?m`, then we assume `e` may contain any free variable
in the local context associated with `?m`.

This mapping enables O(1) local context compatibility checks during metavariable assignment.
Instead of traversing local contexts with `isSubPrefixOf`, we check if the maximal free variable
in the assigned value is in scope of the metavariable's local context.

**Note**: We considered using a mapping `PHashMap ExprPtr FVarId`. However, there is a corner
case that is not supported by this representation. `e` contains a metavariable (with an empty local context),
and no free variables.
